problem: Find the area between the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x)$, the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=-2$ and $y=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Area Bounded by a Curve and the Y-Axis

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Area Bounded Between a Curve and the Y-Axis by First Rewriting the Function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14082348/assets/eb7118486df97c3abae6c8492170090df0c654064799e04826a39a94bcfa22a8.png)

Find the area between the curve $y=\sqrt{x+1},$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{x+1} \\ {y}^{2} & =x+1 \\ x & ={y}^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-y{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-0)-(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-1 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is $\left|-\dfrac{2}{3}\right| = \dfrac{2}{3}.$

Find the area of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=y-{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}^{3} & =0 \\ y(1-{y}^{2}) & =0 \\ y & =0,\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

From the diagram, we see that we want to find the area between the curve $x=y-{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y-{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{2}-0)-(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
